summary: Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard (Doktorgrad under Masatoshi Nagatomi), he also studied under Geshe Wangyal and several Rinpoches, later serving at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (ca. 1972–1998).

Alexander Coburn Soper worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Sinology. He earned degrees from Hamilton College and Princeton University (Ph.D. 1944). He served as a professor at Bryn Mawr College (1946) and New York University (1960), and edited Artibus Asiae (1958–1993).

Alexander Cunningham was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied at Christ's Hospital and Addiscombe Military Seminary, and under James Prinsep. He founded the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as Archaeological Surveyor (1861–1865) and Director-General (1871–1885).

Alexander Dubyanskiy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Moscow Conservatory and Moscow State University (PhD 1970). He taught Tamil language and literature at Moscow State University (ca. 1973–2020) and taught at the Russian State University for the Humanities (ca. 1994–2020).

Alexander Duff worked in religious studies and history and archaeology. He was educated at the University of St Andrews (ca. 1821–1829) and the University of Aberdeen, and taught Krishna Mohan Banerjee.

Alexander Duncan Campbell worked in linguistics and Indology. In 1816, he served on the Board of Superintendence at the College of Fort St. George, and he was active at the Madras Literary Society from around 1818 to 1820.

Alexander Eggers was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer and Leopold von Schroeder. He served at Tallinn Cathedral School (1896–1914), directed Privatlyzeum Greifswald (1919–1928), and taught at Zemkessches Privatlyzeum (1928).

Alexander Faulkner worked in Indology and other fields. He served in the Indian Civil Service as a civil servant from 1839 and was an assistant commissioner in the Customs, Salt, and Opium Department until 1874.
Alexander Freiman studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (ca. 1903–1907) and Christian Bartholomae (ca. 1906–1907).

Alexander Gardner is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Kalamazoo College, Michigan State University, and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. under Donald S. Lopez Jr.), he also studied with Robert H. Sharf and Janet Gyatso, and holds a post at BDRC.

Alexander Hamilton was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu literature at East India Company College (1806–1818). A co-founder of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1823, he taught scholars including Friedrich Schlegel and Franz Bopp.
Alexander Henderson Diack was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Aberdeen (1876–1879) and King's College, Cambridge (1879–1881).
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. A PhD candidate at the University of Toronto, he has served as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated under Christian Friedrich Schwartz and at Göttingen and Lincoln's Inn, he served as Chief Justice in Ceylon and on the Executive Council of Ceylon (ca. 1811–1819), and co-founded the Royal Asiatic Society.

Alexander Kabanoff was a Japanologist and scholar of Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as a senior researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and as head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He held academic posts at Kazan Imperial University (ca. 1826–1849) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (ca. 1849–1870).

Alexander Kingsbury Smith works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at American University, Oxford, and École Pratique des Hautes Études (PhD 2016). His posts include lecturer at University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (2020) and host of Armchair Academics (2021).

Alexander Kinloch Forbes was an Indologist and historian who studied at East India Company College and under Dalpatram. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1862) and founded the Gujarat Vernacular Society and Forbes Gujarati Sabha.

Alexander Lubotsky is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Moscow State University and Leiden University (PhD under Robert S. P. Beekes), he became full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.
Alexander Macmillan is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied at the SIT Graduate Institute under advisor Elizabeth Morrison (attested 2013).
